title: A move changes only the term, and only for ticked customers
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure COD is the shop's default for new customers.
  • Make sure the shop's own term A, due 15 days after the invoice date, is held by exactly three customers, customer A, customer B and customer C (a new term holds only this case's customers), whose names are in that A to Z order, with credit limits of $500.00, $0.00 and $1,000.00.
  • Make sure customer A has a phone number, an address and a sales representative set. Customer D holds Net 20.
  • Start on the Credit Terms page (Settings, then "Credit Terms" in the Finance group), Active tab.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click the "⋯" at the right of the term A row.
  2. Click "Move Customers".
  3. Untick customer C.
  4. Choose "Net 45" in "Move To".
  5. Click "Move 2 Customers".
  6. Open customer A's customer page.
  7. Open customer C's customer page.
  8. Open customer D's customer page.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The menu opens.

Step 2:

  • A window titled "Move Customers from term A" opens.

Step 3:

  • The count reads "2 selected".

Step 4:

  • The button reads "Move 2 Customers".

Step 5:

  • The toast "2 customers moved to Net 45." shows.

Step 6:

  • The term is Net 45.
  • The phone number, address, sales representative and credit limit are exactly as before.

Step 7:

  • Customer C (unticked) is still on term A, with no new note.

Step 8:

  • Customer D is still on Net 20, with no new note.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11673 (Story 4, Move Customers)

  • S4-R18: “Every field other than the credit term (and, under S4-R16, the credit limit) stays as it was on each moved customer.”
  • S4-R19: “Customers not ticked, and customers on other terms, are untouched.”
